findings.evidenceJa: 近寄りがたい緊張感
findings.governingReading: The kitchen is noisy and wrapped in a tense atmosphere that makes it difficult to approach.
findings.explanation: The English turns the interpersonal tension into a generally forbidding atmosphere.

findings.evidenceJa: 険悪ね
findings.governingReading: Illya bluntly calls the atmosphere between Rin and Sakura hostile or ugly.
findings.explanation: The English weakens active hostility into ordinary failure to get along.

findings.evidenceJa: 正気？
findings.governingReading: Illya asks whether Shirou is sane to leave the cooking to the two sisters.
findings.explanation: The English weakens the sharp comic challenge to his sanity.

findings.evidenceJa: キチンと正座して
findings.governingReading: Illya sits properly in formal seiza on the cushion.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the exact posture and its neat propriety with a broad cultural label.

findings.evidenceJa: 随分話し合ったけど
findings.governingReading: Shirou says there was considerable discussion before neither woman yielded.
findings.explanation: The English keeps the impasse but removes the length and prior attempt at negotiation.

findings.highlight: She shouldn’t know the proper etiquette
findings.evidenceJa: 作法を知らないというのに
findings.governingReading: Shirou admires Illya’s elegance even though she does not know the local etiquette.
findings.explanation: The English changes an observed lack of knowledge into the narrator’s expectation that she should not know.

findings.evidenceJa: 始終気にかけてる
findings.governingReading: Illya infers that Rin is paying attention to Sakura constantly.
findings.explanation: The English removes the persistent, continuous quality of Rin’s concealed attention.

findings.highlight: Sakura knows that, so she’s making mistakes she normally doesn’t
findings.evidenceJa: 桜も桜でそれが分かってるから、いつもはしない筈の失敗をしてる
findings.governingReading: Shirou reads Sakura’s uncharacteristic mistakes as symptoms of being unable to stop thinking about Rin.
findings.explanation: The English causal wording makes the mistakes sound like something Sakura produces because she knowingly understands Rin’s attention.

findings.evidenceJa: すくなくとも桜の気持ちだけは分かる
findings.governingReading: Shirou qualifies his insight: he does not know Rin’s feelings, but at least Sakura’s feelings alone he understands.
findings.explanation: The English preserves the contrast but loses the limiting emphasis around the one person he claims to understand.

findings.highlight: she wants Tohsaka to like her
findings.evidenceJa: 好きになって欲しいと思っている筈だ
findings.governingReading: Shirou infers that Sakura must want Rin to love her in return.
findings.explanation: The English removes his explicit epistemic qualification.

findings.highlight: a silence that even gets us nervous
findings.evidenceJa: 見ているこっちの方が息苦しくなる沈黙
findings.governingReading: The sisters’ silence is so oppressive that Shirou, merely watching, feels short of breath.
findings.explanation: The English pluralizes the experiencer and replaces the bodily oppression with generic nervousness.

findings.highlight: Didn’t you want to say something?
findings.evidenceJa: なにかお話があるんですか
findings.governingReading: Sakura asks Rin whether she has something she wishes to discuss.
findings.explanation: The English changes an open question into an assumption that Rin already wanted to speak.

findings.evidenceJa: 他人の味付けって珍しい
findings.governingReading: Rin says another person’s particular seasoning is unusual or novel to encounter.
findings.explanation: The English broadens the concrete interest in seasoning into a truism about cooking differences.

findings.evidenceJa: 普段は人の事情なんてお構いなし
findings.governingReading: Shirou says Rin normally pays no heed to other people’s circumstances.
findings.explanation: The English replaces interpersonal disregard with dominance, changing the trait under discussion.

findings.highlight: she’s reserved when she’s actually with her
findings.evidenceJa: 本人に対してだけ他人行儀
findings.governingReading: Sakura acts formally distant only when addressing Rin herself, despite calling her Nee-san in private.
findings.explanation: The English generalizes the address-based distance into personal reserve and weakens the linguistic mechanism.

findings.evidenceJa: 内緒話がしたかった
findings.governingReading: Shirou says he only wanted a brief private conversation.
findings.explanation: The English copies the Japanese construction into unnatural English suggesting covert speech.

findings.highlight: It’s obvious that you really want to call her that
findings.evidenceJa: ホントはそう呼びたいクセに無理してる
findings.governingReading: Shirou says it is obvious Sakura wants to call Rin Nee-san but is forcing herself not to.
findings.explanation: The English preserves the wish but omits her deliberate emotional restraint.

findings.evidenceJa: かまをかけてみた
findings.governingReading: Shirou says he tried a probing bluff to test Sakura’s reaction.
findings.explanation: The English says he fabricated the underlying claim rather than strategically presenting it as a probe.

findings.evidenceJa: 内気で、恥ずかしがり屋で、姉思いの妹
findings.governingReading: Shirou realizes Sakura is more introverted, bashful, and devoted to her elder sister than he had thought.
findings.explanation: The English compresses three character traits into a vague reserve concerning Rin’s feelings.

findings.highlight: she might think that you hate her
findings.evidenceJa: 嫌われてると思っている節もある
findings.governingReading: Shirou sees indications that Rin may believe Sakura dislikes her.
findings.explanation: The English preserves possibility but removes the evidential nuance that Rin shows signs of this belief.

findings.evidenceJa: 姉と妹の関係
findings.governingReading: Shirou refers to the relationship between an elder sister and a younger sister.
findings.explanation: The English produces malformed possessive phrasing and obscures the reciprocal sibling relation.

findings.highlight: there’s nothing more important than that
findings.evidenceJa: それ以上に確かな関係なんてない
findings.governingReading: Shirou says there is no relationship more certain or dependable than Sakura loving Rin and Rin being her sister.
findings.explanation: The English changes certainty and security into comparative importance.

findings.highlight: there’s so much love that I’m a bit jealous
findings.evidenceJa: 正直、ちょっと妬けるぐらい
findings.governingReading: Shirou guarantees their mutual sisterly love and jokes that, honestly, it is enough to make him a little jealous.
findings.explanation: The English adds a claim about the quantity of love instead of letting the mild jealousy supply the comic measure.

findings.evidenceJa: むん、と力をいれて
findings.governingReading: Sakura visibly steels herself and summons resolve before heading to the kitchen.
findings.explanation: The English invents a breath and removes the compact physical show of determination.

findings.evidenceJa: レタスをちぎってください
findings.governingReading: Sakura asks Rin to tear the lettuce by hand.
findings.explanation: The English changes the preparation technique to cutting.

findings.highlight: I’ll leave the serving to you
findings.evidenceJa: 盛り付けは任せます
findings.governingReading: Sakura entrusts the arrangement and plating of the food to Rin.
findings.explanation: The English changes presentation of the dish into the broader act of serving it.

findings.evidenceJa: 桜って呼び捨てにしてる
findings.governingReading: Rin notes that she already calls Sakura by her bare given name without an honorific.
findings.explanation: The English omits the no-honorific intimacy that supports Rin’s face-saving permission.

findings.highlight: They messed up so many times
findings.evidenceJa: 盛り付けは間違える
findings.governingReading: Their mistakes specifically include getting the plating or presentation wrong.
findings.explanation: The English summarizes the failures and omits the first concrete culinary mistake.

findings.highlight: hot enough to numb your tongue
findings.evidenceJa: 舌がヒリヒリする
findings.governingReading: The mapo tofu makes Illya’s tongue sting or burn.
findings.explanation: The English changes active stinging into numbness.

findings.evidenceJa: 呆れた風にイリヤは言う
findings.governingReading: Illya speaks with an exasperated or fed-up air.
findings.explanation: The English changes weary exasperation into astonished incomprehension.

findings.evidenceJa: 二人が作ったチグハグな料理
findings.governingReading: Shirou gratefully eats the incongruous, poorly coordinated assortment the two sisters made.
findings.explanation: The English removes the mismatch that connects their culinary result to their emotional awkwardness.
